findingDetails.title: doctor.sh hard-codes a five-level walk to .utcp_config.json, so in the vendored packet its only Code Mode check is a guaranteed false negative
findingDetails.scopeProof: the depth is a literal in this file; every invocation available in this repository was enumerated and none reaches the directory that holds the file
findingDetails.claim: doctor.sh resolves .utcp_config.json at a fixed depth that matches only the upstream skill layout, so its MCP registration check cannot see the workspace config in the vendored copy.
findingDetails.counterevidenceSought: Enumerated all three candidate depths from the script directory: three up is the Product Owner root (no file), four up is the workspace root (file present, registers clickup_official), five up, the coded value, holds no file. Ran the script; it printed the not-found line.
findingDetails.alternativeExplanation: The packet may only ever be executed from the upstream layout, where five up is correct. Rejected as complete mitigation: the packet ships scripts/README.md, which tells a reader to run it, and the byte-copy contract makes this copy the only one a Product Owner reader has.
findingDetails.downgradeTrigger: If Product Owner documents that these scripts must only be run from the shared skill repository, the impact becomes a documentation note and the severity drops to P2.
